topPRs.title: docs: regenerate op-reth CLI reference at v2.4.1 via new gen-op-reth-cli pipeline (IA slice 9)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

IA-modernization slice 9 (final slice of the lane) per [`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md): the op-reth CLI regeneration pipeline, plus its first regeneration at `op-reth/v2.4.1`.

## Before / After

**Before:** the 59-page op-reth CLI reference was a one-time snapshot of the retired Vocs site with no regeneration pipeline. It silently drifted from every op-reth release — missing whole command families (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`), documenting seven `db settings set` subcommands the binary no longer has, and carrying stale flags and help text on 51 pages.

**After:** the reference is regenerated from the current finalized release (`op-reth/v2.4.1`) and gains a documented, review-gated regeneration pipeline for future releases. Readers get 21 new command pages (including the whole `proofs` family), 51 corrected pages, and the 7 retired pages redirect to the surviving `db settings set` page that documents the replacement `v2` flow. The hand-written CLI overview gains one table row (`proofs`).

## How

- **Pipeline** — new `docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/` (`main.mjs` + `README.md` + `manifest.json`): a zero-dependency Node port of upstream reth's `docs/cli/update.sh` + `docs/cli/help.rs` (the exact tooling whose output format the original snapshot matches). It walks a pinned release binary's `--help` tree and emits the MDX pages (`diataxis: reference` frontmatter), the docs.json nav fragment for the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group (hand-written `cli/overview` guarded as the group's first entry, never touched), and provenance in `manifest.json`. Environment-dependent help output (home paths, version/target triples, CPU-count defaults) is scrubbed with upstream's replacement set.
- **Provenance chain** — binary built from source at tag `op-reth/v2.4.1` (tag commit `a9a8dad3f15`, the latest finalized non-rc release), which pins upstream reth at rev `f2eecc65482a`. `manifest.json` records `{tag, binaryVersion, sha256-over-generated-tree}`.
- **Idempotency** — running the generator twice against the same binary is a byte-for-byte no-op (verified live: second run reports `0 new, 0 changed, removed 0`, `git status` clean). `--check` mode recomputes the whole tree in memory and fails on any divergence, so hand edits to generated pages cannot survive review.

## No CI wiring (per Matthew's ruling)

Nothing in this diff touches `.circleci/`, `.github/`, or any package script; nothing runs unattended. Regeneration is registered as a **review-gated Mintlify docs automation** (see the README's "Automation registration" section, mirroring the gen-flags precedent in `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`): when a newer finalized `op-reth/v*` tag exists than the manifest's, a regeneration is *proposed for human review* — never merged by CI. All 79 changed files live under `docs/public-docs/`.

## Regeneration drift (first run at v2.4.1)

| Kind | Count | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New pages | 21 | `proofs` family (7 pages), `db copy`, `db migrate-v2`, `db state`, `db prune-checkpoints` (3), `db stage-checkpoints` (3), `db checksum rocksdb`, `db get rocksdb`, `db settings set v2`, `p2p enode` |
| Updated pages | 51 | Genuine drift: new flags (e.g. `--tx-channel-memory-limit`, `--rpc.disable-metrics`, `--rpc-cache.max-bals`), renames (`--enable-discv5-discovery` → `--disable-discv5-discovery`), help-text and `--chain` list changes |
| Deleted pages | 7 | The per-table `db settings set <table>` leaves, superseded upstream by `db settings set v2` |
| Nav entries | 409 → 423 | +21 / −7; all other tabs and groups byte-identical, tab count 8 → 8 |

## Redirects (645 → 652)

| Change | Count | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (R5, one per deleted page) | 7 | `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/db/settings/set/<table>` → `.../db/settings/set` (the surviving parent documenting the `v2` flow) |
| Retargeted in place | 9 | The legacy `/rust/op-reth/cli/.../db/settings/set/<table>` entries (7 + 2 `*_in_static_files`) each pointed at a now-deleted URL; retargeted to `.../db/settings/set` so no chains or stale destinations exist |

Full 652-entry trace: 0 duplicate sources, 0 chains, 0 sources shadowing live pages, 0 destinations pointing at deleted URLs; no prose page links to any deleted URL.

## Deviations from the plan (stated plainly)

1. **7 redirects vs the plan's ~0–5 budget** — the estimate predates further months of upstream drift; every removal is the single superseded `db settings set` per-table family, all covered same-PR per R5 (plus the 9 in-place retargets the no-chain rule requires).
2. **Binary built from source (dev profile) instead of the release Docker image** — the release ships no binary assets and the image registry is egress-blocked in the build environment. Feature set matches the official image build (default features = DockerfileOp set); clap `--help` output is feature-dependent, not profile-dependent. Release metadata was injected exactly as the official image build does.
3. **One fork-specific scrub beyond upstream `help.rs`** — `default: op-reth/<VERSION>-<SHA>/<ARCH>`: the fork identifies as `op-reth/...` where upstream's scrub patterns only cover the `reth/...` spelling; without it the build-host arch would leak into a page. Recorded in `main.mjs` comments and the README.
4. **`manifest.json` carries `binaryVersion`** in addition to the gen-flags-precedent `{tag, sha256}` — extra provenance for a binary-derived generator.

## Verification (re-derived independently by the verifier)

- `--check` against the tag binary: exit 0 — 72 pages, nav fragment, and manifest all match the `--help` tree; manifest sha256 `e979848d9b4a…9017f6ad` re-derived independently and matches.
- `op-reth/v2.4.1` confirmed as the latest finalized (non-rc, non-draft) op-reth release via the GitHub API; `rust/Cargo.toml` at the tag pins reth rev `f2eecc65482a`.
- Sample pages (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`, `node`, `db list`, `config`): flag sets match the binary's `--help` exactly; the 7 deleted commands are absent from the binary (`db settings set` now has only `v2`).
- Leakage sweep over all 72 pages: zero hits for the version string, commit SHAs, build timestamps, target triples, or build-host paths.
- Lints: `validate-nav.ts` OK (424 pages on disk / 423 nav entries / 1 allowlisted orphan — counts reconcile exactly), `validate-redirects.ts` OK (652 redirects, 11 grandfathered — baseline byte-identical to how IA-8 left it), `lint-link-policy.mjs` 0 findings. All 73 touched MDX files compile clean under @mdx-js/mdx.

## Wiz SAST findings (8 LOW) — addressed

Wiz flagged 8 LOW SAST findings on the PR head. The only SAST-scannable code in this diff is `scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/main.mjs` (everything else is MDX/JSON/Markdown), and its sinks account for exactly the two pattern classes Wiz LOW-flags in JavaScript: two `child_process` executions (`execFileSync` for `--help`/`--version`) and six dynamic-path `fs` operations (page write/mkdir/delete, docs.json write, manifest read/write, existing-page reads).

Context: this is a repo-local, review-gated generator that only shells out to a binary the operator explicitly passes via `--bin` (built locally from a release tag); it already used `execFileSync` with argument arrays (no shell), and every dynamic path is rooted at script-relative constants. The one genuine untrusted-input flow — subcommand names parsed from the binary's `--help` output feed both process arguments and file paths — is now hardened in `06bcbc29c9`: names are validated against the shape clap actually produces (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/`, run aborts on anything else), and every page write/delete asserts containment inside the generated tree. No behavior change: `--check` still passes byte-identically at v2.4.1. The remaining dynamic-path reads/writes against script-relative constants (docs.json, manifest.json) are inherent to any generator and not reachable from untrusted input.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Preview: the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group under Node Operators → Reference renders with `overview` first and nested subgroups in `--help` order (eyeball `db settings set` → `set`, `v2`)
- [ ] Spot-check a new page (e.g. `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/proofs`) against `op-reth proofs --help` at v2.4.1
- [ ] Hit a deleted URL (e.g. `.../db/settings/set/receipts`) and confirm the redirect lands on `.../db/settings/set`
- [ ] Confirm the README's automation-registration section matches the intended Mintlify registry entry (review-gated, never CI)
- [ ] Agree the 4 deviations above are acceptable

## Program status

This closes the IA-modernization lane: slices 1–9 have all shipped. D12 is the program's last remaining content slice.

topPRs.title: op-conductor: route raft logs through application logger
topPRs.author: Kemperino
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- route HashiCorp Raft logs through op-conductor's configured application logger
- apply the existing log level and formatting to Raft core, snapshot, and network logs
- preserve Raft subsystem names and severity when forwarding records

## Root cause

`raft.DefaultConfig` defaults to debug logging and creates an independent logger on stderr when no logger is provided. Op-conductor left that logger unset, so Raft logs bypassed `--log.level` and could be classified as errors by log collectors based on their stderr stream.

## Impact

Raft logs now respect op-conductor's configured log level and use the same structured output path as the rest of the service. With the default info level, Raft debug logs are suppressed instead of being emitted independently to stderr.

## Validation

- `just lint-go` (`0 issues`)
- `go test ./op-conductor/...`
- `go vet ./op-conductor/...`
- `go mod tidy -diff`

topPRs.author: claude

<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

Slice 8 of the iteration-2 IA modernization plan (`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md` in ethereum-optimism/solutions): the redirect-bearing hygiene half. This PR holds the serialized docs.json queue slot; IA-9 (the last IA slice, op-reth CLI regeneration) queues behind it.

## Before / After (what readers see)

**Before:** the App Developers "Tools & SDKs" sidebar group mixed two URL namespaces (`app-developers/tools/*` and `app-developers/tools-sdks/*`). Two nav pages had nothing on them: "Profiling the Node" (the single line "Coming soon...") and "Networks" (an empty component that renders nothing). The snap-sync guide sat in the nav under Chain Operators > Archive but lived at a `guides/features/` URL.

**After:** every app-developer tools page lives under `app-developers/tools-sdks/*`, with every old URL redirecting to its new home. The two placeholder pages stop appearing in the nav and their URLs redirect to the pages that actually have the content (Kona node monitoring; OP Mainnet network information). The snap-sync file lives at `chain-operators/archive/snap-sync`, matching where the nav already put it. Zero nav pages under 200 bytes remain (slice 8 success metric met).

## How

- 9 `git mv` moves (8 `tools/*` pages into `tools-sdks/*`, snap-sync into `chain-operators/archive/`), all R100 renames except 5 files whose only content change is a link fix (below).
- 2 deletions: `node-operators/kona-node/faq/profiling.mdx` (52 B stub, no in-tree source material to fill it from) and `app-developers/reference/networks.mdx` (193 B, its only content is the `OPNetworks` component, which is defined nowhere in the repo).
- 12 new redirects, 26 existing redirects retargeted in place (no chained redirects; per rule R5 every moved or deleted URL gets a same-PR redirect).
- 8 inbound prose links updated across 8 files; 4 previously grandfathered dead links inside the moved files fixed; the redirect-lint baseline shrinks 17 -> 11 (it only ever shrinks).
- `diataxis:` frontmatter added to the 2 touched pages that lacked it (`kona-node/faq/overview.mdx`: reference; `chain-operators/tools/proxyd.mdx`: how-to).
- Nav entries: 411 -> 409 (the 2 delistings; all moves are in-place). All other docs.json content is byte-identical: only 3 tabs change, each by exactly the expected entries.

## Per-candidate decisions (fill-or-delist sweep)

| Candidate | Decision | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `app-developers/tools-sdks/op-alloy/glossary` (129 B) | Already closed by dedup slice D13 | File absent at base; redirects to `/op-stack/reference/glossary` already live on develop. Recorded, not redone. |
| `node-operators/kona-node/install/binaries` (177 B) | Already closed by dedup slice D9 | File absent at base; redirects to `/node-operators/kona-node/run/binary` already live on develop. Recorded, not redone. |
| `node-operators/kona-node/faq/profiling` (52 B) | Delist + redirect | Body was the single line "Coming soon...". No user-facing profiling material exists in the vendored kona workspace to fill it from (only Docker build config, Grafana JSON, FPVM allocator internals). Redirects to the monitoring page, the nearest real observability content. FAQ list on `faq/overview` updated. |
| `app-developers/reference/networks` (193 B) | Delist + redirect | Body was exactly one JSX tag, `OPNetworks`; that component is defined nowhere in the repo, so the page renders nothing. A fill would duplicate two canonical pages (connecting-to-op, rpc-providers). Redirects to `/op-mainnet/network-information/connecting-to-op`, matching the existing `/superchain/networks` redirect. The 1 inbound link (quickstarts/get-started) re-pointed. |
| `chain-operators/guides/features/sequencer-defined-metering` | No action (stays hidden) | `hidden: true` pending the Lagoon hardfork, which is still "In development / Not scheduled" per the hardfork registry page. Per the plan's reconciliation, the delist fallback is not taken for an intentionally hidden page. |
| `app-developers/tools/*` (8 pages) | Moved to `tools-sdks/*` | Namespace unification, URLs 1:1, nav positions unchanged. |
| `chain-operators/guides/features/snap-sync` | Moved to `chain-operators/archive/` | URL now matches its nav home (Chain Operators > Archive). |

## Redirects (12 new)

| Source | Destination |
|---|---|

| /app-developers/reference/networks | /op-mainnet/network-information/connecting-to-op |
| /app-developers/tools | /app-developers/guides/building-apps |

## Redirects (26 retargeted in place, sources unchanged; each previously pointed at a URL this PR moves or deletes, so retargeting prevents chains)

| Old destination | New destination | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| /app-developers/tools/faucets | /app-developers/tools-sdks/faucets | /builders/tools/faucets; /app-developers/tools/build/faucets; /app-developers/tools/testing/faucets |
| /app-developers/tools/block-explorers | /app-developers/tools-sdks/block-explorers | /builders/tools/block-explorers; /app-developers/tools/build/block-explorers; /app-developers/tools/infrastructure/block-explorers |
| /app-developers/tools/supersim | /app-developers/tools-sdks/supersim | /stack/interop/tools; /stack/interop/tools/supersim; /interop/tools; /interop/tools/supersim; /app-developers/tools/development/supersim |
| /app-developers/tools/account-abstraction | /app-developers/tools-sdks/account-abstraction | /builders/tools/account-abstraction; /builders/dapp-developers/contracts/account-abstraction; /app-developers/tools/build/account-abstraction; /app-developers/tools/wallets/account-abstraction |
| /app-developers/tools/data/data-and-dashboards | /app-developers/tools-sdks/data/data-and-dashboards | /app-developers/tools/data-and-dashboards; /app-developers/tools/data-and-dashboards/overview |
| /app-developers/tools/data/data-glossary | /app-developers/tools-sdks/data/data-glossary | /app-developers/tools/data-and-dashboards/data-glossary |
| /app-developers/tools/data/analytics-tools | /app-developers/tools-sdks/data/analytics-tools | /builders/tools/analytics-tools; /app-developers/tools/build/analytics-tools |
| /app-developers/tools/data/oracles | /app-developers/tools-sdks/data/oracles | /builders/tools/oracles; /app-developers/tools/build/oracles |
| /chain-operators/guides/features/snap-sync | /chain-operators/archive/snap-sync | /operators/chain-operators/management/snap-sync; /chain-operators/guides/management/snap-sync |
| /node-operators/kona-node/faq/profiling | /node-operators/kona-node/monitoring | /rust/kona/node/faq/profiling |
| /app-developers/reference/networks | /op-mainnet/network-information/connecting-to-op | /app-developers/tools/connect/networks |

Full-array checks (all 645 entries, verified independently by builder and verifier): zero duplicate sources, zero redirect chains, zero stale destinations, zero sources shadowing live pages, and no other redirect anywhere in the array still points at a moved or deleted URL.

## Link fixes riding in the moved files

The 5 non-R100 renames differ from their base blobs only by these link fixes (each link verified dead at base, live at head):

- faucets, block-explorers, data/oracles: `[developer tools overview](/app-developers/tools)` -> `[building apps overview](/app-developers/guides/building-apps)` (the successor page every retired tools-hub redirect already points to).
- supersim: `/app-developers/tutorials/development/supersim` (no page at that directory) -> `.../supersim/first-steps` (real page).
- data-and-dashboards: its data-glossary link updated to the moved URL.

## Flags for reviewers (deliberate judgment calls)

1. **A 12th, consequential redirect not literally enumerated in the plan:** `/app-developers/tools -> /app-developers/guides/building-apps`. Deleting the emptied `tools/` directory turned 2 grandfathered `/app-developers/tools` links (in `rpc-providers.mdx` and `op-stack/introduction/op-stack.mdx`, files otherwise untouched) into new lint findings. The hub redirect resolves both and matches the exact precedent of `/app-developers/tools/overview`, `/app-developers/tools/build`, and `/app-developers/tools/tools`, which all already point at building-apps. Total is 12 redirects against the plan's ~15 budget.
2. **The 5 `app-developers/reference/tools/supersim/*` pages are not moved.** The plan's scope sentence unifies `app-developers/tools/*` into `tools-sdks/*`; these five live under `reference/tools/` and sit in the nav under App Developers > Reference > Supersim (the accepted reference subgroup from slice 4), so the acceptance criterion "one namespace under Tools & SDKs" is met without them. Moving them would be 5 extra moves + 5 redirects for no nav change; left alone.
3. **snap-sync destination path** is `chain-operators/archive/` (a new one-page directory) rather than the sibling pattern `chain-operators/tutorials/archive/`. Chosen because the page is a how-to, not a tutorial, and the plan asks for "an archive path to match its nav home", which is the tab-level Archive group.

## Verification

- `validate-redirects.ts` with `DOCS_LINT_BASE_REF=develop` (deleted-page check active): OK, 645 redirects, 11 grandfathered violations remaining (baseline shrank 17 -> 11; every removed entry corresponds to a violation genuinely fixed in this diff).
- `lint-link-policy.mjs --baseline`: 0 findings.
- All 17 touched .mdx files compile clean under MDX v3.
- Adversarial verifier pass re-derived every claim from source: rename detection, full redirect-array trace, whole-repo inbound-link sweep for all 12 retired URLs, docs.json semantic diff (untouched tabs byte-identical), and the Lagoon gate for the hidden SDM page.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] The three flags above are acceptable as ruled, or say the word and any of them is trivially reversible.

topPRs.title: docs: normalize leading-slash nav slugs to bare style (IA slice 7)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

IA slice 7 of the docs-improver iteration-2 plan (`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md` in ethereum-optimism/solutions) — the zero-redirect half of audit move 8. Independently verified by an adversarial pass (all 83 line pairs audited programmatically, lints re-run, Lagoon gate re-derived).

## Before / After

**Reader-visible change: nothing.** This is pure slug-style hygiene. `docs.json` navigation stops mixing two slug styles — 83 entries written as `"/op-stack/..."` alongside 328 written bare (`"op-stack/..."`) — which has been a recurring source of tooling confusion (greps, nav diffs, scripts that compare slugs). Mintlify resolves both styles to the same URL, and the repo's own nav validator normalizes leading slashes before comparing (`normalizePath` in `scripts/lint/common.ts`), so:

- Zero URL changes
- Zero redirects added, removed, or retargeted (633 before and after, byte-identical array)
- Nav entry count unchanged: 411 before, 411 after; same slug multiset after normalization; zero duplicates

## How

Mechanical transform: walk `navigation.tabs[].groups` (recursively through nested `pages`) and strip the leading `/` from string page entries. `redirects`, `navigation.global`, and every other key untouched — redirect `source`/`destination` strings correctly keep their leading slashes per Mintlify convention. The file round-trips byte-exactly through `JSON.stringify(d, null, 2) + "\n"`, and the committed diff is exactly 83 removed/83 added lines where every hunk is adjacent `-"/op-stack/..."` / `+"op-stack/..."` pairs with identical indentation and trailing commas (verified programmatically over the full `-U0` diff, not by sampling). Distribution of the 83 at base: 69 in the Protocol tab, 14 in Get Started (the glossary + Contribute pages moved there by IA slices 1–2 after the plan census, slugs unchanged).

## Orphan ruling: `sequencer-defined-metering` stays hidden

The slice's second item (re-home the orphan `chain-operators/guides/features/sequencer-defined-metering.mdx` into nav) is governed by the plan's cross-lane reconciliation: the re-home applies only if the gating hardfork has shipped; otherwise the page stays hidden and the PR records the check. Re-derived at base `b6eb77b1` (current `develop`):

- `op-stack/protocol/hardforks/lagoon.mdx` frontmatter: `hardfork_lifecycle: development`
- Registry-generated facts (`snippets/generated/hardforks/lagoon.mdx`): Mainnet activation "Not scheduled", Sepolia activation "Not scheduled"

Lagoon has **not** shipped, so the stay-hidden branch applies: no nav entry added, and the slice-8 delist-and-redirect fallback is **not** queued (the plan explicitly rules it out for an intentionally hidden page). The page remains allowlisted in `scripts/lint/nav-allowlist.json` with a matching reason ("Add to the Chain Operators > Guides > Features nav group when the feature ships"); no allowlist change needed.

## snap-sync: noted for slice 8

The `chain-operators/guides/features/snap-sync` URL vs its nav home (Chain Operators > Archive) mismatch is recorded here as known debt, per the plan's accept-or-note item. The file move and its 1 redirect are slice 8's scope.

## Nav-count reconciliation (plan's conditional 415 vs measured 411)

The plan predicted 415 **if** slices 1–6 landed exactly as planned (411 at plan baseline `40a649dc` + 2 IA-4 index pages + 1 IA-5 index page + 1 re-homed orphan here). Measured slug-set diff `40a649dc` → `b6eb77b1`: 14 slugs removed and 14 added — the IA index-page additions are offset by dedup-lane merges/renames/cuts (D6, D7, D9, D13) and the 5 notice archive moves, which the plan's arithmetic did not model — netting to 411. This slice's orphan +1 is not taken (stay-hidden branch above). So the enforced acceptance criterion is the plan's "unchanged with the fallback recorded" branch: 411 → 411, leading-slash 83 → 0.

## Lints (re-run independently at `bb97e9dc`)

```
nav validator: OK — 412 pages on disk, 411 distinct nav entries, 1 allowlisted orphan(s)   (identical output at base)
redirect lint: OK — 633 redirects, 454 files scanned, 17 grandfathered violation(s) remaining
lint-link-policy: 0 finding(s), clean (baseline empty before and after)
```

### Rand is unsound with a custom logger using rand::rng()
[GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
It has been reported (by @​lopopolo) that the `rand` library is [unsound](https://rust-lang.github.io/unsafe-code-guidelines/glossary.html#soundness-of-code--of-a-library) (i.e. that safe code using the public API can cause Undefined Behaviour) when all the following conditions are met:

- The `log` and `thread_rng` features are enabled
- A [custom logger](https://docs.rs/log/latest/log/#implementing-a-logger) is defined
- The custom logger accesses `rand::rng()` (previously `rand::thread_rng()`) and calls any `TryRng` (previously `RngCore`) methods on `ThreadRng`
- The `ThreadRng` (attempts to) reseed while called from the custom logger (this happens every 64 kB of generated data)
- Trace-level logging is enabled or warn-level logging is enabled and the random source (the `getrandom` crate) is unable to provide a new seed

`TryRng` (previously `RngCore`) methods for `ThreadRng` use `unsafe` code to cast `*mut BlockRng<ReseedingCore>` to `&mut BlockRng<ReseedingCore>`. When all the above conditions are met this results in an aliased mutable reference, violating the Stacked Borrows rules. Miri is able to detect this violation in sample code. Since construction of [aliased mutable references is Undefined Behaviour](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/nomicon/references.html), the behaviour of optimized builds is hard to predict.

#### Severity
Low

#### References
- [https://github.com/rust-random/rand/pull/1763](https://redirect.github.com/rust-random/rand/pull/1763)
- [https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0097.html](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0097.html)
- [https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc)
